text:
sasha: Quick triage note: HF->internal conversion of windfall9b + our int4 profile yields a surprising drop on summarization and next-token KL. Looks like an architecture layout mismatch rather than pure quant noise.
ryan: How bad is the drop? numbers?
sasha: Short smoke numbers (summary bench):
```
windfall9b-fp16      R1 0.46  PPL_next 8.9  latency/token 12.1ms
windfall9b-int4      R1 0.35  PPL_next 13.2 latency/token 5.9ms
windfall9b-int4-rotfix R1 0.41 PPL_next 10.2 latency/token 6.1ms
```
sasha: So full int4 degrades quality a lot; applying a per-head-aware rotary fix recovers a chunk.
ekta: Per-head-aware? Did converter preserve head_map/per_head_dims? Weve seen converters collapse heterogenous head layouts into uniform groups.
sasha: Exactly. HF metadata had a per_head_dims vector (some heads 32, some 16, some 48). Converter normalized to uniform 32 across groups and dropped explicit head_map.
mattie: That will shift sin/cos indexing. Our sincos table index = head_index * head_dim_offset, so wrong mapping rotates the wrong subvectors.
j: (ryan) Also check kv-cache stride: if the cache was written assuming uniform stride but runtime projections are hetero, reads will be misaligned and amplify quant error.
sasha: I dumped a tiny header diff:
```
# upstream: per_head_dims: [32,32,16,48,...]
# converted: head_groups: [16,16,16,16]  -> uniformized
# converted: head_map: omitted
```
ekta: Concrete plan: 1) quick mitigation - run quant with rotary disabled (fall back to absolute positional proj) to see if quality improves without fixing converter. 2) longer fix - change converter to carry per_head_dims + head_map through and produce a mapping table that runtime uses when building sin/cos and cache strides.
jules: For the mitigation, also try hybrid: compute sincos per-head using the *converted* mapping but keep head ordering shuffles to match projection layout (i.e., remap at runtime). Might be cheaper than full converter change.
mattie: Also run a logit-delta/topk histogram between fp16 and int4 across 500 prompts - that will show if mass shifts to EOS or common stop tokens (hallucination vs terse answers).
sasha: Scheduling runs now:
- 1755600000-01: int4 quant with rotary-disabled (quick bench)
- 1755600000-02: reconvert-preserve-headmap + int4 (longer)
- 1755600000-03: topk-logit-diff + KL per-token (500 prompts)
bench-bot: Jobs queued: 1755600000-01..03. Estimated 30-120m depending on queue.
ekta: Add a synthetic micro-test: single-token continuation for 10k random seeds, compute per-step KL to catch steady drift. If reconversion fixes things, add a CI unit test that generates random head_map and verifies sin/cos indices map back to projection offsets.
ryan: If reconversion is nontrivial, we should at least gate auto-quant for models where converter normalized head dims. Emit a warning in console and skip int4 by default for those models.
jules: Also check tokenizer edgecases - sometimes vocab remap + byte normalization interacts badly with quantized LM leading to punctuation shifts; include a small token-preservation check in the runs.
sasha: Noted, I'll include token-preservation and add a sample prompt that had the worst R1 drop for manual inspection.
mattie: One more thought: try an int4 profile that uses per-channel calibration (rather than global) for projection matrices - might soften sudden shifts if the misalignment is only amplifying quant noise.
sasha: Good idea. Adding a 1755600000-04 for per-channel-int4 calibration quick smoke.
bench-bot: Queued 1755600000-04.
ryan: Great. Post results here when done, include logit histograms and an example divergent completion. We'll decide whether to ship a runtime fallback or prioritize converter patch.
sasha: Will update. Thanks all :satellite:
